claims.claim: Right now, two things from the Sun's core are reaching the Earth. (Hook, A4: all a viewer who swipes at second two takes away.)
claims.source_checked: https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml (NASA MSFC 'The Solar Interior', last updated 14 Jan 2025); https://arxiv.org/pdf/1508.05379 (BX-P, full text)
claims.note: MSFC: the core's reactions 'release the energy that ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'; neutrinos 'pass right through the overlying layers of the Sun and, with some effort, can be detected here on Earth'. BX-P: neutrinos 'travel almost undisturbed from the core of the Sun to the surface of the Earth'. Both reach the Earth continuously; 'the Earth', not 'you', so it also holds at night. A viewer who leaves at second two keeps only this sentence, which is true; it does not claim sunlight photons come from the core.

claims.claim: 2 THINGS, 1 CORE (two lanes from one drawn core: straight teal, tangled coral, ending at a photo of the Earth; tagged NOT TO SCALE)
claims.note: Same claim as 1. Zones drawn at CORE = 0.25 R and RADIATIVE = 0.70 R, matching MSFC ('from 25% of the distance to the surface to 70%'). The diagram carries 'NOT TO SCALE' on every Lanes card.

claims.claim: One left the core about eight minutes ago.
claims.source_checked: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/sunfact.html (last updated 9 May 2024); https://physics.nist.gov/cgi-bin/cuu/Value?c; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41567-021-01463-1 (KATRIN, Nat. Phys. 18, 160, online 14 Feb 2022)
claims.note: Recomputed: radius 695,700 km / c = 2.32 s; (149.6e6 km - radius) / c = 496.7 s = 8.28 min; 8.14 to 8.42 min over the year (147.1e6 to 152.1e6 km). Total about 8.3 min. KATRIN 'upper limit of m_nu < 0.8 eV c^-2 at 90% CL': at 10 keV, gamma > 1.25e4 and 1 - v/c < 3.2e-9, so neutrinos travel at c here. 'About eight minutes' holds.

claims.claim: 8 MINUTES AGO; teal clock tag 8 MIN
claims.note: 8.3 min rounded to 8; the tag sits on the neutrino (teal) lane.

claims.claim: The other left it tens of thousands of years ago, maybe far more.
claims.source_checked: https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/11084 (NASA SVS 'Origin of Light'); https://articles.adsabs.harvard.edu/pdf/1992ApJ...401..759M (Mitalas & Sills, ApJ 401, 759-760, doi:10.1086/172103; both scanned pages read); https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml
claims.note: SVS: 'Over the course of 40,000 years it will be absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly until reaching the sun's surface'. MS92 abstract: '1.7 x 10^5 yr for the diffusion time scale of the present Sun', and the common 3 x 10^3 to 3 x 10^4 yr estimates are 'much too short'. MSFC: 'an individual photon takes about a million years to finally reach the interface layer'. Lowest cited figure 4e4, others 1.7e5 and 1e6: 'tens of thousands, maybe far more' is true at each (A3). What left is the energy; MSFC: 'This energy diffuses outward by radiation ... and by convective fluid flows'. Stix (2003) not opened; nothing spoken rests on it alone.

claims.claim: 40,000+ YEARS AGO; coral clock tag 40,000+ YEARS
claims.note: 40,000 is the lowest cited figure (SVS); the '+' is supported by MS92 (1.7e5, and its rejection of anything up to 3e4 as too short) and MSFC (~1e6).

claims.claim: Both start where hydrogen fuses into helium.
claims.note: MSFC: 'The Sun's core is the central region where nuclear reactions consume hydrogen to form helium. These reactions release the energy that ultimately leaves the surface as visible light.' BX-P eq. (1) gives the neutrinos from the same conversion.

claims.claim: HYDROGEN → HELIUM; CORE circled on the SDO 304 A photograph; CORE DRAWN AT 1/4 OF THE RADIUS
claims.where: on-screen: HYDROGEN → HELIUM / CORE / CORE DRAWN AT 1/4 OF THE RADIUS
claims.source_checked: https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml; public/cutout/sunlight/sun304.jpg viewed; public/SOURCES.json entry (NASA/SDO AIA, 19 Aug 2010)
claims.note: MSFC: the core extends to '25% of the distance to the surface or 175,000 km from the center'. The circle is 0.25 of the cut-out disc radius (545 px). The cut-out includes a little off-limb glow: the visible 304 A disc is about 508 px in radius, so the circle is about 27% of it. Within the label's 'drawn at 1/4' as a drawing; no change needed.

claims.claim: Every second, the Sun turns over four million tonnes of its mass into energy.
claims.note: NSSDC: 'Mass conversion rate (10^6 kg/s) 4260.' = 4.26 million tonnes/s. Check: 'Luminosity (10^24 J/s) 382.8' / c^2 = 4.259e9 kg/s. 'Four million' rounds down; the energy carried by neutrinos (~2%) would only raise it.

claims.claim: 4 MILLION+ TONNES; A SECOND · 4.7 MILLION US TONS; counter '... TONNES SO FAR' at 4.26 million tonnes per second of video
claims.where: on-screen: 4 MILLION+ TONNES / A SECOND · 4.7 MILLION US TONS / TONNES SO FAR
claims.note: 4.26e9 kg / 907.185 kg = 4.70 million short tons. Counter uses the fact-sheet rate, rounded to the thousand.

claims.claim: And every time four hydrogen nuclei become one helium nucleus, two neutrinos are made.
claims.note: BX-P: 'the “effective reaction” that takes place is the conversion of hydrogen (p) into helium (He), 4p → 4He + 2e+ + 2νe'. Holds for both the pp chain and CNO (same net reaction). A hydrogen nucleus is a proton.

claims.claim: 2 NEUTRINOS; 4 H → 1 He + 2 e⁺ + 2 ν; drawing: four H discs spiral in and merge in one flash into one He disc, then two ν streak out of the He nucleus
claims.where: on-screen: 2 NEUTRINOS / 4 H → 1 He + 2 e⁺ + 2 ν / H / He / ν (Fusion card)
claims.source_checked: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1508.05379 eq. (1) and Fig. 1 (pp chain); https://solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml; index.tsx Fusion component
claims.note: The equation is right (BX-P eq. 1). The drawing is not: it shows four nuclei fusing in a single collision and both neutrinos leaving the finished helium nucleus. BX-P Fig. 1 and MSFC ('In the first step two protons collide to produce deuterium, a positron, and a neutrino. In the second step ... In the third step ...') describe a chain of two-body steps, with the neutrinos made in the steps, not by the helium nucleus. The script itself later relies on 'fusion's very first step'. Unlike the other drawings, this card carries no SCHEMATIC / NOT TO SCALE tag (A6). Change: add an on-screen tag such as 'NET RESULT OF SEVERAL STEPS' (or 'SCHEMATIC: NET REACTION') to the Fusion card, and say so in SOURCES claim 6; or redraw it as steps.

claims.claim: Neutrinos barely interact with anything.
claims.note: BX-P: 'they can only interact via the weak force. Thus, they travel almost undisturbed from the core of the Sun to the surface of the Earth'. MSFC: they 'pass right through the overlying layers of the Sun'.

claims.claim: BARELY INTERACT (straight teal lines from the Sun's centre out through the photograph)
claims.note: Straight unbroken lines through the Sun match 'almost undisturbed' / 'pass right through'.

claims.claim: They fly straight out of the Sun in about two seconds.
claims.note: 695,700 km / 299,792.458 km/s = 2.32 s from the centre; ~1.7 s from the core's edge at 0.25 R (MSFC). Speed = c to < 1e-8 (KATRIN < 0.8 eV). 'Straight': BX-P 'almost undisturbed'. 'About two seconds' holds.

claims.claim: ABOUT 2 SECONDS; clock running 0.0 S to 2.3 S as the teal line is drawn centre to surface
claims.note: 2.32 s shown to one decimal as 2.3 S.

claims.claim: Eight minutes later, they reach the Earth, and pass through you.
claims.note: Surface to Earth 496.7 s = 8.28 min (8.14-8.42 over the year). 'Pass through you': BX-P 'travel almost undisturbed ... to the surface of the Earth'; claim 23 shows how few are stopped.

claims.claim: 8 MINUTES LATER (teal lines through the ISS photograph of sunrise over Earth's limb)
claims.source_checked: as claim 17; public/cutout/sunlight/sunrise.jpg viewed; public/SOURCES.json entry (NASA ISS047-E-138450)
claims.note: Rounded 8.3 min. Lines pass straight through the Earth in the photo, consistent with BX-P.

claims.claim: Tens of billions of them cross every square centimetre of you, every second.
claims.note: BX-P: measured pp flux '(6.6 ± 0.7) × 10^10 cm−2 s−1, consistent with the SSM prediction'; SSM values 5.98 and 6.03 x 10^10. Nature abstract: pp neutrinos 'constitute nearly the entirety of the solar neutrino flux'. 66 billion = tens of billions.

claims.claim: TENS OF BILLIONS; PER CM² (0.16 SQ IN), PER SECOND; 1 cm² (ENLARGED); SCHEMATIC (dots streaming through a square)
claims.where: on-screen: TENS OF BILLIONS / PER CM² (0.16 SQ IN), PER SECOND / 1 cm² (ENLARGED) / SCHEMATIC
claims.note: 1 cm^2 = 0.155 sq in -> 0.16. The 60 dots are not a count and the card says SCHEMATIC; the square says ENLARGED.

claims.claim: In Italy, a detector called Borexino counted the ones from fusion's very first step.
claims.note: BX-P: 'Borexino [16] is a liquid scintillator detector located at the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso, in central Italy'; pp neutrinos are 'those produced in the top left of the chain, whose parents are simply two protons'. Nature: 'The primary reaction is thought to be the fusion of two protons ... Here we report spectral observations of pp neutrinos'. MSFC: 'In the first step two protons collide to produce deuterium, a positron, and a neutrino.' 'Counted': results are reported in counts per day; the rate comes from a spectral fit, which the script does not contradict.

claims.claim: BOREXINO, ITALY; drawing of a sphere of liquid with a ring of light sensors inside a tank, tagged SCHEMATIC
claims.note: BX-P: liquid scintillator, light 'collected by photomultipliers (PMTs) surrounding the inner detector', 'Outside the inner detector, a water tank'. The drawing matches that layout and is labelled SCHEMATIC.

claims.claim: In every hundred tonnes of its liquid, it caught about a hundred and forty a day.
claims.note: BX-P eq. (2): 'R_pp = 144 ± 13 (stat) ± 10 (syst) (d · 100 t)−1'; fit 'pp Q: 144 ± 13'. Per-100-t is a normalised rate (fiducial mass 75.5 t; the scintillator holds more than 100 t), so 'in every hundred tonnes' is correct. 'About a hundred and forty' for 144.

claims.claim: ABOUT 140 A DAY; PER 100 TONNES (110 US TONS); tally marks with a flash per catch counting up to 144 A DAY (AVERAGE)
claims.where: on-screen: ABOUT 140 A DAY / PER 100 TONNES (110 US TONS) / 144 A DAY (AVERAGE)
claims.note: 100 t / 0.907185 = 110.2 short tons. The tally is the per-100-t rate (the card's sub-label says PER 100 TONNES) and is marked AVERAGE; the drawing is marked SCHEMATIC, so individual flashes are not presented as identified events (BX-P: 14C background '∼ 40 (s · 100 t)−1, four orders of magnitude larger').

claims.claim: The energy takes the slow road.
claims.note: Minutes against tens of thousands of years or more. No new number. On screen: THE SLOW ROAD, coral random walk drawn, NOT TO SCALE.

claims.claim: It is absorbed and given off again, over and over, then carried up by churning gas.
claims.note: SVS: 'absorbed by other atoms and emitted repeatedly until reaching the sun's surface'. MSFC: energy crosses the radiative zone by radiation, then 'by convective fluid flows (boiling motion) through the convection zone, the outermost 30%'; 'convective motions carry heat quite rapidly to the surface'. 'Churning gas' = convection in the (ionised) gas.

claims.claim: OVER AND OVER (random walk to 0.70 R, then convection loops to the surface; NOT TO SCALE)
claims.where: on-screen: OVER AND OVER / THE SLOW ROAD
claims.note: Walk stops at RADIATIVE = 0.7 R, convection above it, as MSFC. Step size is not to scale and the card says NOT TO SCALE.

claims.claim: Tens of thousands of years later, maybe far more, it leaves the surface as sunlight.
claims.source_checked: as claim 5; MSFC 'ultimately leaves the surface as visible light'
claims.note: Same figures and hedge as claim 5.

claims.claim: Year counter climbing to 40,000+ YEARS and stopping
claims.note: Stops at the lowest cited figure and adds '+'.

claims.claim: Eight minutes after that, it lands on your skin.
claims.note: Photosphere to Earth 488-505 s (8.1-8.4 min).

claims.claim: 8 MINUTES LATER; coral tag + 8 MIN
claims.note: As claim 30.

claims.claim: So the sunlight shows what the core was doing when that energy set out. (On screen: SUNLIGHT: THEN, 40,000+ YEARS AGO.)
claims.where: spoken; on-screen: SUNLIGHT: THEN / 40,000+ YEARS AGO
claims.note: Follows from claims 5 and 7 (the core's energy is what leaves as sunlight, after the transit). BX-P states the same reasoning: the SSM 'assumption ... that the photon and neutrino luminosities from the Sun can be correlated; i.e., that the Sun has been stable for the past 10^5 years'.

claims.claim: The neutrinos show what it was doing eight minutes ago. (On screen: 8 MINUTES AGO, NEUTRINOS.)
claims.note: 2.3 s out of the Sun plus 8.3 min to Earth.

claims.claim: In twenty fourteen, Borexino's count matched what the sunlight predicts, to within about ten percent.
claims.note: BX-P: expected rate '131 ± 2 (d·100 t)−1 (assuming the high-metallicity SSM)'; measured 144 ± 13 (stat) ± 10 (syst); flux 'consistent with the SSM prediction'. 144/131 = 1.10 and the measurement's error is 16.4/144 = 11%, so 'matched to within about ten percent' is accurate. 'What the sunlight predicts': BX-P says the agreement 'justifies the assumption made by the SSM that the photon and neutrino luminosities from the Sun can be correlated'; Nature abstract: the pp neutrinos show 'about 99 per cent of the power of the Sun, 3.84 × 10^33 ergs per second' comes from pp fusion. Data taken Jan 2012-Jun 2013, result published 2014.

claims.claim: WITHIN ABOUT 10%; bars from zero, PER DAY, PER 100 TONNES: SUNLIGHT PREDICTS 131, BOREXINO COUNTED 144 ± 16
claims.where: on-screen: WITHIN ABOUT 10% / PER DAY, PER 100 TONNES / SUNLIGHT PREDICTS / BOREXINO COUNTED / 131 / 144 ± 16
claims.note: 131 from BX-P (high-metallicity SSM; low-metallicity scales to ~130). 144 ± 16: sqrt(13^2 + 10^2) = 16.4. Bars share a zero baseline at 3.6 px per count, so their heights are honest.

claims.claim: So the core is burning about as hard now as when today's sunlight set out.
claims.note: BX-P: 'the present measurement of the pp neutrino flux is consistent with expectation justifies the assumption made by the SSM that the photon and neutrino luminosities from the Sun can be correlated; i.e., that the Sun has been stable for the past 10^5 years.' BX-P's 10^5 yr is its transit time; the script states the same inference against the transit time without a number, which keeps it consistent with claim 5's hedge. 'About as hard' = within the ~10% of claim 34.

claims.claim: ABOUT THE SAME
claims.note: As claim 36.

claims.claim: The sunlight on your skin is old news. The neutrinos are fresh. And they agree. (On screen: OLD NEWS, FRESH, THEY AGREE.)
claims.where: spoken; on-screen: OLD NEWS / FRESH / THEY AGREE
claims.note: Restates claims 5, 17 and 34. No new number.

claims.claim: How many neutrinos do you think passed through you while you watched this? (On screen: YOUR GUESS?)
claims.note: A question, not a claim. Its presupposition (neutrinos passed through the viewer during the video, day or night) holds: 6.6e10 per cm^2 per second, almost undisturbed through the Earth.

claims.claim: The picture that stands for 'you' at the foot of both lanes (SOURCES: 'a CC0 photograph of a hand, which stands for "you"'; 'the hand that stands for you')
claims.where: on-screen: the 'you' photograph (Lanes, 8 MINUTES LATER card)
claims.source_checked: src/shorts/age-of-sunlight-long/index.tsx (const SUNRISE / SUNRISE_WIDE, You component; hand.jpg is not referenced); public/cutout/sunlight/sunrise.jpg viewed; public/SOURCES.json
claims.note: The render does not use the hand: 'you' is public/cutout/sunlight/sunrise.jpg, NASA ISS047-E-138450, orbital sunrise over Earth's limb (public domain). The picture itself makes no false claim, but the SOURCES block describes a visual that is not in the short (A1/A6). Change the script's 'Not spoken' paragraph to say 'a NASA photograph from the ISS of sunrise over the Earth (ISS047-E-138450), which stands for "you"' and drop 'the hand that stands for you' / 'a CC0 photograph of a hand'. Or switch the composition to hand.jpg.

claims.claim: SOURCES: 'The fusion card is labelled "4 H → 1 He + 2 ν" (claim 6)'
claims.source_checked: index.tsx Fusion: <Tick text="4 H → 1 He + 2 e⁺ + 2 ν">; script SOURCES claim 6 and closing paragraph
claims.note: The screen shows '4 H → 1 He + 2 e⁺ + 2 ν' (correct, BX-P eq. 1, and as SOURCES claim 6 says), but the closing 'Not spoken' paragraph quotes it without the positrons. Change that paragraph to '4 H → 1 He + 2 e⁺ + 2 ν' so the SOURCES block describes what is on screen.
